question.worked_solution:
First, we decompose all of the terms into their various factors. The $2(x-1)$ in the numerator becomes $2\cdot (x-1),$ and the $2(x+1)$ in the denominator becomes $2\cdot (x+1).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2(x-1)}{2(x+1)}=\frac{2\cdot (x-1)}{2\cdot (x+1)}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we cancel out all the pairs of common factors in the numerator and denominator. In this case, there is only one pair of $2$'s.

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\frac{2\cdot (x-1)}{2\cdot (x+1)} & = \\ \frac{\cancel{2}\cdot (x-1)}{\cancel{2}\cdot (x+1)} & = \\ \frac{(x-1)}{(x+1)}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the expression simplifies to $\frac{x-1}{x+1}.$
